minutes.headline: Commissioners agreed to hold a special meeting to award the water main bid, and to waive finance charges for a hardship customer.
minutes.summary: The Water District commissioners discussed the upcoming bid opening for a water project and agreed to post a special meeting the following Wednesday so the engineer can present the bids for award. They approved the August 9th minutes, agreed to waive finance charges for a hardship customer on a payment plan, and reviewed a health insurance buyback policy. A commissioner reported on the Select Board meeting about PFAS and private wells.

budget_items.what_was_said: Bids will be checked for bond, certified check and item math before award; the board wants the engineer to present the bids.

budget_items.topic: Customer past-due balance and finance charges
budget_items.what_was_said: A customer with large bills from leaks has had her balance reduced by an assistance payment, but monthly finance charges eat into what she can pay. Board favored waiving finance charges if she keeps to a payment plan.
The assistance agency typically pays a standard amount per applicant, with occasional larger payments.
The average regular bill was mentioned as part of the payment plan.

budget_items.topic: PFAS private well testing and filtration costs
budget_items.what_was_said: Cost of a certified test and of a filtration system for private wells was discussed; the Board of Health felt funding was premature.
The district's funding request was ranked fairly high among several requests; a decision is expected in about two weeks.
A revised buyback policy pays out at the end of the fiscal year, prorated if an employee leaves, and can be ended by commissioners with 30 days notice.

decisions.decision: Agreed to post a special meeting for the Wednesday after bids open so the engineer can present the bids and the board can award.
Agreed to waive finance charges for the hardship customer as long as she keeps current on her regular bill and sticks to a fixed payment plan.
Health insurance buyback policy to take effect this year, immediately.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed to post a special meeting for the Wednesday after bids open, so the engineer can present the water project bids and the board can award.
Commissioners agreed to waive finance charges for a hardship customer, on condition that she keeps current on her regular bill and keeps to a fixed payment plan.
The board agreed that a revised health insurance buyback policy takes effect this year; it pays at fiscal year end, prorated if an employee leaves, and can be ended on 30 days notice.
A commissioner reported on the Select Board meeting about PFAS and private wells; the Board of Health felt funding for well testing and filtration was premature.
A motion to accept the August 9th minutes was made; the outcome was not audible in the recording, and no recorded votes appear in the minutes.
